procurement_preference: GCP Marketplace (mandated for new vendors); open to AWS Marketplace only if GCP listing timeline slips.
interested_skus_notes: Private deployment SKU via marketplace procurement; wants add-on for extended audit log retention + compliance packet availability. Asked if Private can be purchased as a private offer with annual commit and billed via marketplace.
requirements_summary: Regulated fintech evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) for EU workloads. Key requirements: EU data residency (Frankfurt preferred), customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK/KMS integration), detailed audit logging with export to SIEM, configurable retention controls (esp. request/response payload handling), SSO/SAML for Console, and a marketplace-ready security packet (SOC 2 / ISO-aligned).
workload_and_performance_notes: Initial workload: 2 internal apps (fraud investigation summarization + agent assist). Expect bursty weekday load. Target p95 end-to-end < 900ms for short responses; for longer summaries p95 < 4s. Strong sensitivity to 'noisy neighbor' risk -> prefers dedicated capacity inside Private deployment (or clear isolation story). Needs streaming + structured output for downstream case system ingestion.
data_residency_notes: They require processing + storage in EU. Asked specifically: (1) which regions are available for control plane vs data plane, (2) whether any telemetry leaves EU by default, (3) how to pin region per org/project, (4) how failover behaves if EU region is degraded (must not silently fail over to US).
encryption_kms_notes: Hard requirement: customer-managed keys for data at rest (KMS). Asked if Redwood supports: per-tenant key separation, key rotation, envelope encryption, and the ability to revoke keys and validate data becomes inaccessible. Also asked about TLS versions/ciphers and whether mTLS is supported for private endpoints.
audit_logging_notes: Needs audit logs covering: org/user admin actions, API key lifecycle, model configuration changes, routing/fallback policy updates, and access to any retained artifacts. Must support export to their SIEM (Splunk) and minimum 1-year retention (they can store; want Redwood to retain at least 90 days by default or provide configurable retention). Requested example audit log event schema for review.
retention_and_data_handling_notes: Security team asked: default retention for prompts/outputs, whether payloads are stored at all in Private, ability to disable payload logging, and how long operational metadata is retained. They will likely mandate: zero retention of prompt/output content, or explicit opt-in with short TTL for debugging. Also asked about backups/snapshots and whether customer can control retention windows.
shared_responsibility_questions: Asked for a one-pager explaining shared responsibility for Private: what Redwood operates vs what Helio operates (networking, IAM, key mgmt, logging sinks). Requested clarity on who has access to what in incident response (Redwood SRE access paths, break-glass controls).
